wwox_observation: [DATO, Cheng 2020] In global Wwox-null preweaning pups ethosuximide lowered the provoked-seizure stage, mostly after minute 30; it is significant in the knockout and not significant in wild-type and heterozygous pups (one-way ANOVA; no genotype-by-treatment test exists or can be computed from the figure); wild-type stage is about 1 on a 0 to 6 scale, near the floor; the age of the test is not stated in the paper or its supplement (searched). One experiment, one laboratory. [INFERENZA, by eye and by measurement of the figure] The early-window drop looks proportionally similar in all genotypes; the knockout difference is late, when wild type is already near the floor.
mechanism_and_missing_bridge: Knockout-selective suppression (reading E1) needs a drug-by-genotype interaction at a stimulus where wild type is above the floor and at an age at which the agent can act. A difference in significance is not an interaction. T-type mediation is NOT part of this hypothesis (see E4).
probe_or_qualified_compound: Ethosuximide, named by the source; class: antiseizure agent with a contested T-type mechanism. No compound is proposed for any use.
action_cell_context: Provoked-seizure assay in global Wwox-null pups (+/+, +/-, -/-) of one age, the same session, a vehicle per genotype; the assay age, the stimulus and the doses are the laboratory's; the design is the in vivo brief of 2026-11-18.
competing_alternative: E2 age-limited with a wild-type floor; E3 a general anticonvulsant effect proportional in every genotype; E4 a T-type route; the lithium pattern (an effect in all three genotypes, INV-09) is the contrast case.
favourable_result: Effect ratio in the knockout at most 0.7 with an interval excluding 1; wild type null (interval inside 0.85 to 1.15); interaction ratio at most 0.7 or at least 1.43; assay-sensitivity panel valid at the age; wild type above the floor.
weakening_result: Interaction ratio between 0.7 and 1.43 with a valid panel (a general effect); a wild-type effect at an older age only (E2); no effect anywhere (not replicated at this age and stimulus); a failed panel is an assay failure, not a negative.
next_decision: A pilot first: the variability of the 60-minute summary on the scale of the primary analysis, the assay age and a stimulus that gives wild type a measurable response; then the size. The published effect size cannot power the interaction (SCI bracket from the figure: about 180 to 320 animals per cell at the paper's stimulus with wild type at the floor; about 70 to 220 per cell if wild type had the knockout's variability, IT arithmetic, INFERENZA); the interaction is exploratory unless the pilot finds a low-variability summary.

wwox_observation: [DATO, abstract level, one Prague laboratory family] In the rat ethosuximide was effective against PTZ only from about 25 days of age and not at 18 days or younger (Mares and Velisek 1983, 1987; Mares 1998). The mouse ontogeny of ethosuximide against PTZ was not found by two routes (HE, ADV-052 part d). One mouse pup datum for another seizure type goes the other way (Cortez 2004, SSADH-null pups P10 to P21: absence-like seizures abolished; abstract only, the age of the drug test not stated, a spontaneous GHB and GABA-B-driven model, not PTZ). Cheng's pups are 'preweaning', the test age not stated. [INFERENZA] The rat age floor is unresolved for the mouse and may be endpoint-bound.
mechanism_and_missing_bridge: Age-limited effect with a wild-type floor: a null in +/+ and +/- pups is what a young-age effect predicts whatever the genotype.
probe_or_qualified_compound: Ethosuximide, and reference agents with different age profiles as an assay-sensitivity panel, named as class examples from the rodent literature only (ADV-054, ADV-064): a flat-profile general anticonvulsant (protective against PTZ at every age in the rat, mouse not found), a rising-profile agent, a falling-profile NMDAR-subunit-selective agent (GluN2B-selective agents fade across P7 to P18); diazepam is not age-flat in the rat.
action_cell_context: Wild-type pups at the assay age and at two or more older ages inside the window to about P28, the same stimulus and scale; knockouts at the assay age only (they cannot be matched at older ages).
competing_alternative: E1 and E3; the panel's own validity at each age is a precondition, not a result.
favourable_result: Wild-type null at the assay age and an effect at an older age while the panel is valid at both ages.
weakening_result: The same effect at every wild-type age (E3), or the panel fails at the assay age: move the age, do not read the null.
next_decision: State the assay age against the age windows of the panel agents; report the panel per age.

wwox_observation: [DATO, abstract level] Ethosuximide is a classic anti-PTZ and anti-absence agent in adult rodents (ADV-051 package A) but not a general anticonvulsant: it lowered the pilocarpine threshold in rats (Turski 1987), was ineffective or of low potency against kainate, and lacked action in guinea-pig amygdala kindling. [INFERENZA] A proportional effect in every genotype is the pattern a general property gives; lithium shows that pattern in the one experiment held.
mechanism_and_missing_bridge: A general anticonvulsant effect proportional in every genotype: the Wwox-null adds magnitude, not specificity.
probe_or_qualified_compound: Ethosuximide (named by the source); no compound proposed for any use.
action_cell_context: The same assay and the same genotype-crossed design as E1.
favourable_result: Similar effect ratios in the three genotypes (interaction ratio between 0.7 and 1.43) with a valid panel.
weakening_result: A clear genotype difference (E1) or an age-dependent wild-type effect (E2).
next_decision: The interaction cannot be sized at the variability the published curves show; the order of hypotheses of the brief (panel validity, ratios by genotype and age, then the interaction as an exploratory interval) is the fallback.

wwox_observation: [DATO, search result not biological absence] No T-type current, no Cav3 expression in thalamic or reticular neurons and no Cav3-isoform measurement exists in any WWOX system (two routes, PubMed and Europe PMC; four held WWOX-deficient transcript sets disagree and none samples the thalamus or measures a current; HE, ADV-052). The cell pharmacology of ethosuximide is contested (Leresche 1998, full text read by HE: no effect on the low-threshold calcium current in 10 to 18 day rat thalamic slices; the persistent sodium current down by about 60 percent). A selective-blocker design exists elsewhere (Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 knockout with a selective blocker in a maximal-electroshock assay, abstract level, TRANSFER); no pup datum for the selective blockers was found.
mechanism_and_missing_bridge: T-type mediation of the ethosuximide effect needs a premise nobody has measured; the ethosuximide arm rests on a descriptive pattern, not on a T-type rationale in WWOX deficiency.
probe_or_qualified_compound: A selective T-type blocker class beside ethosuximide, 'selective' by the laboratory's own criterion (published selectivity at the exposure used and published rodent brain exposure); the clinical-stage T-type agent of the ranking inherits none of this as T-type evidence for WWOX.
action_cell_context: The same genotype-crossed, age-matched assay with the selective blocker in the same layout and an engagement control if the laboratory can add one.
competing_alternative: E1, E2, E3 (a pattern shared by the selective blocker would still not prove a T-type route without engagement or genetics).
favourable_result: The selective blocker reproduces the ethosuximide pattern in the knockout (a T-type route is plausible, not proven).
weakening_result: The selective blocker has no effect where ethosuximide has one, or its exposure was inadequate (no engagement control exists in pups: a null is not interpretable without one).
next_decision: A Cav3 current or expression measurement in Wwox-null neurons of the thalamic and reticular circuit, or an isoform-selective blocker with genetics, before any T-type claim.
